registry/poap/calldata-PoapBridge.json — no compilable formats in descriptor — format `mintToken(uint256 eventId, uint256 tokenId, address receiver, uint256 expirationTime, bytes signature)`: format `mintToken(uint256 eventId, uint256 tokenId, address receiver, uint256 expirationTime, bytes signature)` field[4] path `#.eventId` has terminal type `uint256` and is `visible:"never"` — every signed non-address operand must be shown. Hidden bytes, arrays, tuples, packed words, and scalars can change transaction semantics; dbgen cannot classify them as harmless from their type or argument name. Only an exact `address` already surfaced by another visible field/tokenPath may carry `visible:"never"`.
registry/quickswap/calldata-QuickSwap.json — PARTIAL FORMAT DROP: format `removeLiquidityETHWithPermit(address token, uint256 liquidity, uint256 amountTokenMin, uint256 amountETHMin, address to, uint256 deadline, bool approveMax, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s)`: format `removeLiquidityETHWithPermit(address token, uint256 liquidity, uint256 amountTokenMin, uint256 amountETHMin, address to, uint256 deadline, bool approveMax, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s)`: parameter #1 (`liquidity`) is neither rendered, explicitly hidden (`visible:"never"`), nor fully surfaced by a scalar-address `tokenPath` — every contract-call argument must be accounted for so the trusted display cannot omit an effect-bearing field. An indexed/sliced tokenPath covers only one endpoint, not an entire signed array/bytes route (audit H-3)
